title: Captions Pricing 2026: All Five Plans Compared
summary: Captions pricing offers five plans with different costs and limits. See what each plan includes to choose the right fit for your AI video editing.
body_markdown:
## Captions pricing versus CapCut, Descript and VEED


Of the three tools with confirmed prices, Captions Basic is the Entry plan.


The input had no numbers or product names, so this may be a truncated sentence. If so, send the full text and I'll rewrite it properly.


Activepieces has a free plan with unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, and Plus is $20 a month, with each run costing 1 credit however many steps it has, with AI steps costing extra depending on the model, so the 1,000 free credits don't stretch as far if AI is involved.


Only the entry-plan prices I could confirm appear in the table. VEED is left out because I have no price for it I can stand behind.

Read the last column first, because it shows what a yearly commitment buys. Compare tiers only after you decide whether you'll commit for twelve months.


### When Captions costs more


Captions costs more when you pay month to month. Basic on monthly billing is about 84% above its yearly rate, which is $54.84 over a year.


In dollars, Descript's yearly discount is larger. Hobbyist falls from[$24 to $16](https://www.descript.com/pricing) , cutting the monthly cost by a third. Creator falls from $35 to $24.


Business drops from $65 to $50, so a team that skips the annual plan pays $180 more per year on that tier alone.


Captions is cheaper when you can commit for a year and your volume fits the plan's caps. At $5.42, Basic costs about a third of Descript Hobbyist ($16) and of CapCut Pro ($15) on yearly billing.


### Against paying for human captioning


Hire people to caption and you pay per video minute, with rates running from[$1.50 at Speechpad to $2.59 at CaptionSync](https://support.rev.com/hc/en-us/articles/18893487380365-Pricing) , which means longer projects cost proportionally more. GoTranscript charges $1.58 and Rev $1.99, keeping both services similarly priced.


viz type=stackrank title="What human captioning costs per video minute" unit="$ per minute" source="Rev -[https://support.rev.com/hc/en-us/articles/18893487380365-Pricing".58](https://support.rev.com/hc/en-us/articles/18893487380365-Pricing) a minute at GoTranscript to Captioned by people, a 10-minute video costs $15.00 to $25.90. By the time a creator finishes one project this way, they've spent 1.5 to nearly 3 times the cost of the cheapest monthly software subscription.


**Less than seven minutes of captioning is all** it takes for the software to pay for itself: Captions Basic at $9.99 equals about 6.7 minutes of[Speechpad](https://www.speechpad.com/captions) work, so users can absorb the cost on their first job.


Use humans for the few videos where accuracy is non-negotiable, and use the subscription for everything else.
